scope: Independent local review of derived numbers and parser source only; no raw trace/stat/latency re-derivation, Oracle access, compilation or target execution
decision: Published numeric conclusions match the derived rows; document parameter coverage and sender-utilization scopes were clarified

high_scope.normalization: actual variable warmup plus measurement N for CPU/PMU/syscalls; measurement N divided by 20 for throughput
high_scope.interpretation: descriptive closed-loop pipeline changes, not isolated server capacity or formal fixed-cohort acceptance

syscall_parameter_scope: All observed syscall kinds and entered/completed/error/return counts are represented in the four derived trace rows.

Selected parameter counts are aggregates over completed calls: fd roles/flags/iovec/control lengths and poll nfds/timeout class/interests. They do not preserve full per-call arguments or correlations between every field and result.
The one pending ppoll per window is preserved as a PID-to-call-name entry; its argument body is not copied into JSON.
The F receive iovec/control counts equal successful receives, not every completed receive including EAGAIN. Full failed-receive argument coverage cannot be established from these aggregates.
Raw full traces remain private; no raw reparse or parameter reconstruction was performed in this review.
document_fixes: State the per-query and throughput/latency denominators explicitly.
Qualify 99.60–99.89 percent sender CPU as high plain only; list the different PMU and strace ranges.
Replace broad parameter-retention wording with selected completed-call aggregates and pending names, reserving full arguments to private traces.
